chunks: From him, via this chain of narrators, he said:

A man came to him [the Imam] having hired an animal; it perished. He acknowledged that it had completed the agreed time, so he was held liable for the value of the animal, but no hire fee was imposed on him. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This is consistent with the view of the general public (Ahl al-Sunnah), but we do not act upon it. Our practice is based on what we have previously stated: that whenever the animal completes the time, the hirer is liable for the value of the animal and the hire fee is due. The discussion on this has already preceded, and what is narrated next adds clarification to it:
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on liability and hire fees if a hired animal dies after completing the agreed rental period?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights a key jurisprudential divergence in *ijarah* (leasing) regarding liability for accidental loss: while the general view (*al-'ammah*) exempts the hirer from the hire fee if the animal perishes after fulfilling the time, Shia jurisprudence holds that the hirer remains liable for both the animal's value and the full hire fee. Shaykh al-Tusi cites Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saymari to affirm this stricter stance, emphasizing that the obligation of *kirā'* (rent) persists alongside the guarantee (*daman*) of the asset's value, reflecting a distinct interpretation of risk allocation in contractual obligations.
